this is one of my favorite jokes ever. a lot of you probably know it already but I'm sure some don't.

if you want to retell it, it works really well if you can put on some kind of an accent (the guys can be any nationality, really; any accent you can do) and really act it out with some nice pacing and hand gestures and stuff. get people into the story.

once upon a time there were two old friends walking along a lonely Scottish road: Angus and McCloud.

they were discussing life, love, religion, politics -- all the things men of their day and age used to discuss -- when, all of a sudden, McCloud claps Angus on the back and says, "ahhhh, Angus... this road...! I built this road with my own, two, hands. stone by stone. mile by mile. but, do they call me...McCloud the Roadbuilder?! NO."

and Angus tries to console his friend, "but McCloud, you know that in life, you're never really known for the things you accomplish. you have to accept that, in life, you won't ever be recognized for these things. you have to know that, in your heart, truly, these are the things that make you who YOU are; that define YOU as a person."

McCloud ponders this for a moment. he nods his head noncommittally, and they continue on their way.

some time later, they come to a bridge crossing a wide river. and just as they step onto the bridge -- just as they put their first foot on the first plank -- again, McCloud claps Angus on the back and says, "aahhhhh, Angus... this bridge...! I built this bridge with my own, two, hands. plank by plank. nail by nail. but, do they call me...McCloud the Bridgebuilder?! NO."

Angus is a little tired of his friend's nonsense, and he replies simply, "you know what man, deal with it; I don't want to hear the same story again."

McCloud ponders this for a moment. he nods his head noncommittally, and they continue on their way.

finally, they come to their destination. an old pub. and just as they enter the building -- just as they cross the threshhold of the door -- McCloud claps Angus on the back one last time and says, "aaahhhh, Angus.... THIS PUB..! I built this pub with my own, two, hands! brick by brick. stone by stone. floor by floor. pane by pane. shingle by shingle BUT DO THEY CALL ME, MCCLOUD, THE PUBBUILDER?!?

No.

...

...

but ya fuck one goat..."

and that, fellow voaters, is The Goatfucker Joke.
